question: Visualize the p-value and effect size (log2FC) distributions from the provided MeRIP-seq and proteomic data, and perform a chi-square test to evaluate the association between m6A modification status and differential gene expression using the m6A status and DEG status columns already provided in the MeRIP-seq data.

files.eval_guideline: The chi-square p-value must match the reference within two orders of magnitude; whitespace and numeric formatting may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Identical filenames and .txt formats indicate the chi-square test p-value output for the association between m6A status and DEG status.
files.strategy_reasoning: The output is a single chi-square p-value, so numeric comparison is appropriate despite differences in whitespace or numeric formatting. A relative absolute error tolerance of 99 permits values up to 100 times the reference, although it cannot enforce the reciprocal lower bound required by a strict two-orders-of-magnitude comparison.

files.eval_guideline: 2x2 panel figure with log2FC on x-axis; the three individual panels (top-left, top-right, bottom-left) are single-dataset histograms with frequency/count on the y-axis, while the bottom-right panel is an overlaid normalized density comparison of all three datasets (y-axis is density, not frequency); panel labels, colors, bin sizes, and fonts may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Identical filenames and .png image formats correspond to the requested effect size (log2FC) distribution visualization.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires a 2×2 figure with three individual log2FC count histograms and one overlaid normalized density comparison of all three datasets. comparison_details.explanation: Both images contain a 2x2 arrangement showing proteomic, m6A methylation, and gene-expression log2FC histograms, followed by an overlay of all three datasets. The individual panels show broadly consistent patterns: proteomic effects have a relatively broad central distribution, m6A effects have a narrower peak slightly above zero, and gene expression has a sharp peak near zero with long tails. Different bin widths plausibly explain much of the difference in individual histogram heights; exact underlying data equivalence cannot be established visually. The critical discrepancy is the bottom-right panel: the reference overlays normalized probability densities, whereas the candidate overlays raw frequencies and explicitly labels the y-axis Frequency. Because the candidate reports 3,850 proteomic observations versus 12,754 observations in each other dataset, its overlay confounds sample size with distribution shape and makes the proteomic distribution appear disproportionately small. This violates the explicit density-comparison requirement and changes the scientific interpretation. The candidate also omits the reference's dashed zero-effect lines, although zero remains identifiable from its axis ticks. Colors, fonts, and axis limits are otherwise acceptable differences. Neither figure contains p-value distributions or chi-square results, so those broader task components cannot be assessed from these effect-size figures.
